task: Creative track: Hearth & Horizon story from the BIBLE proposal 'The band above the steps'

doc_friction.issue: The salt-weathering proposal said its key terms were unused in overlap.mjs, but 'rising damp' and the sharp-front capillary model were already used by The Tide Mark That Climbed (merged the same day), as was the 'a sealing gift makes it worse' arc; I only found it by running overlap.mjs on 'rising damp' and 'capillary' myself. Proposals should list the mechanism's neighbours, not only its headline words.
The proposal asks for poultices 'over two winters'; poulticing needs drying weather, so the story does it over summers.

deviations.why: Proposal says poultices over two winters; poultices dry in warm weather.
deviations.did: Poultices run over summers; the story ends after one summer's three cycles, with the second still to come.
deviations.result: Consistent with the conservation practice the note cites.

deviations.did: Landed text and pages without audio, as the prompt directs.

notes: Project: Hearth & Horizon (headline shelf). Piece: the-band-above-the-steps (about 4,800 words of story plus closing notes), Dumfries 2051-53, salt weathering from de-icing salt, drying-front band, silane sealant detaching the face, sand/drain/poultice fix. Differentiated from The Tide Mark That Climbed by using its model only as a ratio (h ~ 1/sqrt(E)) and centring salt budget, Correns crystallisation pressure and the de-icer trade-off. All weekdays and Lent/Easter claims computed in code (Easter 2051-04-02, 2052-04-21, 2053-04-06). Also added a new Hearth & Horizon proposal (pitot tube blocked by a wasp nest at a gliding club) since the shelf's Next up was empty. Checks: node bible_done.mjs, node generate.mjs, node --test in ventures/hearth-and-horizon: 20/20 pass. Audio skipped: du total 577 MB.
